detailed_description: Margin Calculator helps you compare cost, selling price, gross profit, profit margin, and markup in one browser-based worksheet. Enter a cost and a selling price to calculate profit as a currency amount, profit margin as a percentage of selling price, and markup as a percentage of cost. The quick target margin and target markup shortcuts can also fill the selling price from your current cost. Use it for simple pricing checks and scenario comparisons; it does not import product catalogs, apply taxes or discounts, or pull live supplier data.
usage_steps: Enter the cost amount for the item or service.
Enter the selling price you want to test.
Click Calculate to show profit, profit margin, markup, and gross profit.
Use a target margin shortcut if you want the tool to calculate a selling price from cost.
Use a target markup shortcut when your pricing rule starts from cost plus a markup percentage.
Review the formula section to confirm whether you need margin or markup for your workflow.
usage_examples: Check whether a $50 cost and $100 selling price produces the expected margin.
Find the selling price needed for a 30% margin on a known cost.
Compare margin and markup before sharing a price estimate.
Explain the difference between margin and markup in a small business worksheet.

faqs.question: What is the difference between margin and markup?
faqs.answer: Margin compares profit to selling price. Markup compares profit to cost. The same cost and price can produce very different percentages.

faqs.question: Can it calculate a price from a target margin?
faqs.answer: Yes. Keep the cost field set, then click one of the target margin buttons to fill the selling price and update the results.

faqs.question: Does it include taxes, fees, or discounts?
faqs.answer: No. The current calculation uses only the cost and selling price fields, so add those adjustments to your inputs if they matter.

faqs.question: Does this connect to accounting or inventory data?
faqs.answer: No. It is a manual calculator for quick pricing scenarios in the browser.
